mainTopic: Lung colors, textures, and tests that decide whether an animal is a טרפה, and whether damage inside the lung counts as a missing piece.
overview: This amud finishes a ruling about a defect on the back of the lung, then goes through many lung conditions. רפרם rules that a lung 'like a chip of wood' is a טרפה, and several opinions explain what that means. רבא says a lung dark like eye shadow is כשרה but black like ink is a טרפה, because black is red that went bad. Green and red lungs are כשרה, proven from two stories of רבי נתן about babies whose ברית מילה was delayed until they recovered. רב כהנא and רב סמא add more appearances: liver-like and leek-green are כשרה, while meat-like and yellowish shades are a טרפה. רבינא and רב יוסף then give hands-on tests for a sealed spot and for a whistling lung, using a feather, saliva, or lukewarm water. Finally, a lung that turned to liquid, or wasted away inside, is כשרה if the outer skin and airway tubes are whole. רבי אבא's challenge from the משנה is answered with the view of רבי שמעון. A new ruling begins at the very end and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: On the back of the lung, even a tiny defect makes it a טרפה
steps.stepSummary: The previous ruling ends: if the defect is on the back of the lung, even something as small as a myrtle leaf makes the animal a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if it is on the back of the lung, even if it is as small as a myrtle leaf, the animal is a טרפה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ruling that started just before this line. It says that when the problem is on the back of the lung, there is no minimum size.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אבל ('but') tells us this is the second half of a distinction. In another spot on the lung a small defect could be tolerated, but on the back even a myrtle-leaf-sized one makes the animal a טרפה. Location changes the rule, not just size.

keyTerms.meaning: On its back (the back side of the lung)
A myrtle leaf, used here as a very small size
An animal with a fatal defect, which may not be eaten even if slaughtered properly

phrases.english: But if it is on its back,
phrases.notes: This finishes a ruling from just before; 'its' means the lung.

phrases.english: even as small as a myrtle leaf – it is a tereifa.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a distinction that began before this section of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A defect on the back of the lung makes the animal a טרפה no matter how small, even the size of a myrtle leaf.

steps.title: A lung like a chip of wood is a טרפה
steps.stepSummary: רפרם rules that a lung that resembles a chip of wood makes the animal a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רפרם says: A lung that is like a chip of wood makes the animal a טרפה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ruling begins. רפרם says a lung that is 'like wood' is a טרפה, but he does not explain in what way it is like wood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This opens a new topic: the overall condition of the lung, not a specific hole or growth. Because 'like wood' is unclear, the next step brings several opinions about what he meant.

keyTerms.meaning: A chip or piece of wood
That resembles, that is similar to

phrases.english: Rafram says:
This lung that is similar to a chip of wood – it is a tereifa.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ruling about the overall condition of the lung.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A lung that resembles a chip of wood makes the animal a טרפה.

steps.title: Different views on what 'like wood' means
steps.stepSummary: Several opinions explain רפרם's comparison: like wood in color, in hardness, swollen, light, or completely smooth with no lobes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say the lung looks like wood. Some say it feels hard like wood. Some say it is swollen. Some say it is light. Some say it is smooth, with no divisions into lobes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lists different explanations of רפרם's ruling. Each one picks a different way a lung can be 'like wood'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רפרם's words were short, so later teachers understood them differently. The first two views are about look versus touch. The last three describe specific physical states: puffed up, light and airy, or one smooth piece with no separate lobes.

keyTerms.meaning: Feel, how it feels to the touch
Lobes, the sections of the lung

steps.confusionAlert: These are not arguments about the halacha of a wooden lung. Everyone agrees that a lung 'like wood' is a טרפה. The disagreement is only about which kind of lung counts as 'like wood'.

phrases.english: There are those who say: in its appearance,
and there are those who say: in its feel.
There are those who say: that it is swollen,
and there are those who say: that it is light,
and there are those who say: that it is smooth,
that it has no sectioning of lobes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the unclear comparison in רפרם's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'wood-like' lung is defined differently: by color, by hardness, as swollen, as light, or as smooth with no lobes.

steps.title: Dark like eye shadow is כשרה; black like ink is a טרפה
steps.stepSummary: רבא separates two dark colors: a lung dark like eye shadow is כשרה, but one black like ink is a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא says: If the lung is dark like eye shadow, it is כשרה. If it is black like ink, it is a טרפה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new ruling about lung color. He draws a line between 'somewhat dark' and 'truly black'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not every dark color is a problem. Eye-shadow dark is fine, but ink-black makes the animal a טרפה. The reason comes in the next step.

phrases.english: Rava says:
Like eye shadow – it is kosher,
like ink – it is a tereifa,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the wood-like lung to the lung's color.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A lung dark like eye shadow is כשרה; a lung black like ink is a טרפה.

steps.title: Why black is bad: it is red that went bad
steps.stepSummary: רבא's ruling is supported by רבי חנינא, who teaches that black is really red that has decayed.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי חנינא says: Black is really red, only it has gone bad.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason for רבא's ruling that an ink-black lung is a טרפה. It quotes רבי חנינא, who says black is spoiled red.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If black is decayed red, then a black lung shows that the lung itself is rotting. That is a real defect, so the animal is a טרפה. Eye-shadow dark is not that far gone, so it stays כשרה.

keyTerms.meaning: That was damaged or went bad

phrases.english: As Rabbi Ḥanina says:
Black is red, except that it decayed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source and reason for רבא's ruling about an ink-black lung.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's ruling that an ink-black lung is a טרפה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי חנינא's teaching that black is red that has decayed.

steps.title: Green and red lungs are כשרה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules that a green lung and a red lung are both כשרה, and says this is learned from רבי נתן.
steps.simpleTranslation: A green lung is כשרה, learned from רבי נתן. A red lung is כשרה, learned from רבי נתן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two more color rulings: green and red are both fine. It says the source is רבי נתן, which sets up the story in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike black, green and red do not show that the lung is rotting. Both rulings point to the same source, a story told by רבי נתן, which comes next.

phrases.english: Green – it is kosher, from the episode of Rabbi Natan.
Red – it is kosher, from the episode of Rabbi Natan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of lung colors, now ones that are permitted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A green lung and a red lung are both כשרה, based on רבי נתן's episode.

steps.title: רבי נתן and the red baby who survived his ברית
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells how רבי נתן told a woman whose two sons died after מילה to wait until her red third son's blood settled; she did, and he lived.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נתן said: I once went to the cities overseas. A woman came to me whose first son died after his מילה, and her second son died too. She brought me her third son. I saw that he was red, and I told her: My daughter, wait until his blood is absorbed into him. She waited, then did the מילה, and he lived. They named him נתן הבבלי after me.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא to prove that a red lung is כשרה. The story shows that a red baby was not doomed; he just needed time and then he was fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The baby's redness came from blood that had not yet settled into his body. Once it settled, he healed and survived the מילה. So redness is a condition that can heal, not a sign of a fatal defect, and a red lung is therefore not a טרפה.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching from the time of the משנה that was not included in the משנה
Until his blood is absorbed into him

steps.whyThisMatters: This story shows how the גמרא learns animal halachos from real cases with people: if a color can heal in a living baby, it is not a sign of a fatal defect in an animal's lung.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita:
Rabbi Natan says:
Once I went to the cities overseas,
one woman came before me
who circumcised her first son and he died,
the second, and he died,
the third – she brought him before me.
I saw that he was red,
I said to her: My daughter,

phrases.aramaic: הַמְתִּינִי לוֹ עַד שֶׁיִּבָּלַע בּוֹ דָּמוֹ.
phrases.english: wait for him until his blood is absorbed into him.
She waited for him and circumcised him, and he lived,
and they would call him
Natan the Babylonian, after my name.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source promised by 'מדרבי נתן' in the previous step.
steps.raayaObject: The ruling that a red lung is כשרה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which רבי נתן tells of a red baby who survived his מילה once his blood settled, showing that redness can heal.

steps.title: רבי נתן's second story: the pale baby who waited for his blood
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן tells of a woman in Cappadocia whose two sons died after מילה. Her third son was green and had no blood. He told her to wait until the blood came in, and then the baby survived his מילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another time I went to Cappadocia. A woman came to me whose first and second sons died after their מילה. She brought her third son to me. I saw he was green, I looked closely, and he had no blood for the ברית. I told her: My daughter, wait until his blood comes into him. She waited, then circumcised him, and he lived. They named him נתן הבבלי after me.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting רבי נתן's ברייתא with his second story. This one is about a green baby, and it is the source that a green lung is כשרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7's story about the red baby showed that redness can settle down. This story shows the same thing about green: the baby's green color was a temporary weakness that went away. In the same way, a green lung is not a sign of fatal damage, so the animal is כשרה.

keyTerms.meaning: Green, meaning a pale, sickly color
The blood that comes out at a ברית מילה

steps.whatToRemember: The two stories of רבי נתן, the red baby and the green baby, are the source that both a red lung and a green lung are כשרה.

phrases.english: And once again, another time, I went
to the province of Cappadocia,
and a woman came before me
who had circumcised her first son, and he died,
the second, and he died;
the third she brought before me.
I saw that he was green.
phrases.notes: "Green" here means pale and sickly looking. This is the link to the green lung.

phrases.english: I looked closely at him
and he did not have the blood of the covenant in him.
phrases.notes: He means the baby didn't have enough blood yet to safely go through a ברית מילה.

phrases.english: I said to her: My daughter,

phrases.aramaic: הַמְתִּינִי לוֹ עַד שֶׁיִּפּוֹל בּוֹ דָּמוֹ,
phrases.english: wait for him until his blood comes into him.
She waited for him, circumcised him, and he lived.
And they would call him
Natan the Babylonian, after my name.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְשׁוּב פַּעַם אַחַת הָלַכְתִּי לִמְדִינַת קַפּוֹטְקְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא of רבי נתן with a second story, this time supporting the green half of the ruling in step 6.
steps.raayaObject: The ruling in step 6 that a green lung is כשרה
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי נתן's story of the green, bloodless baby who survived his מילה after waiting

steps.title: A lung like liver is kosher, a lung like meat is not
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא rules that a lung that looks like liver is כשרה, but one that looks like plain meat is a טרפה. He gives a פסוק as a memory aid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: If the lung looks like liver, it is כשרה. If it looks like meat, it is a טרפה. Your memory aid: "meat in the field that is torn (טרפה)."
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא adds another rule about how a lung looks. Liver-like is fine, but meat-like makes the animal a טרפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is the look and texture of the lung. Looking like liver is acceptable, but looking like ordinary meat means the lung has lost its normal nature. The פסוק is not the source of the law, only a trick to remember which one is the טרפה: "meat" goes with "טרפה".

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with a fatal defect, which is forbidden to eat

steps.confusionAlert: The פסוק here is only a memory aid (סימן). It is not a proof from the תורה for this ruling.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said:
If it looks like liver, it is kosher;
if it looks like meat, it is a tereifa.
And your memory aid is:
"And meat that is torn in the field (tereifa)."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the color discussion, a new statement about the lung's appearance and texture.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A lung that looks like liver is כשרה; a lung that looks like meat is a טרפה.

steps.title: Yellowish shades that make a lung treif
steps.stepSummary: רב סמא בריה דרבא rules that a lung colored like dodder, like saffron, or like egg yolk makes the animal a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב סמא, son of רבא, said: A lung that looks like dodder, or like saffron, or like the color of an egg, is a טרפה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב סמא בריה דרבא lists three yellowish-green colors that make the lung a טרפה, even though a "green" lung was called כשרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 said a green lung is כשרה. Here we learn that not every greenish or yellow shade counts as that kosher green. These three shades are treated as a טרפה.

keyTerms.meaning: Egg (here, the yellow of the yolk)

phrases.english: Rav Sama, son of Rava, said:
This lung that looks like dodder,
or like saffron,
or like an egg, is a tereifa.
phrases.notes: He means the yellow color of the egg yolk.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב סַמָּא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא: הַאי רֵיאָה דְּדָמְיָא כִּכְשׁוּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the green-is-כשרה ruling from step 6 by listing yellowish shades that are a טרפה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A lung colored like dodder, saffron, or egg yolk is a טרפה.

steps.title: So which green is the kosher green?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if all these greenish-yellow shades are a טרפה, what does the kosher green lung look like?
steps.simpleTranslation: But the green lung that is כשרה, what does it look like?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question. Since so many greenish shades were just called a טרפה, it wants to know what the kosher green looks like. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 said green is כשרה, and step 10 just ruled out several green-yellow shades. So the גמרא needs a clear picture of exactly which green is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: What does it look like? / What is the case?

phrases.english: But the green one that is kosher, what does it look like?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raised because step 10 seems to leave little room for the kosher green from step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact shade of green that is כשרה

steps.title: Leek-green is the kosher green
steps.stepSummary: The kosher green lung is the color of leeks.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like leeks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the kosher green is leek-green.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets the line: a true deep green like a leek is כשרה, while the yellowish shades from step 10 are a טרפה. Now both rulings fit together.
steps.whatToRemember: Green like a leek is כשרה. Yellowish colors like dodder, saffron, or egg yolk are a טרפה.

phrases.english: Like leeks.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question in step 11.

steps.title: How to check a sealed spot in the lung
steps.stepSummary: רבינא explains what to do when part of the lung does not fill with air. Cut it open. If there is pus, the pus caused the blockage and the animal is כשרה. If there is no pus, put a feather or saliva on the cut and blow: if it moves or bubbles, it is כשרה; if not, it is a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: If there is a sealed spot in the lung, we bring a knife and cut it open. If there is pus inside, the pus surely caused it, and it is כשרה. If not, we put a feather or saliva on it. If it bubbles, it is כשרה; if not, it is a טרפה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא opens a new topic: a spot in the lung that won't fill with air. He gives a step-by-step test to decide whether the animal is כשרה or a טרפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Finding pus gives an innocent reason for the blockage, so the lung itself is fine. Without pus, we test whether air still reaches the spot. Air that moves the feather or bubbles the saliva shows the lung works, but no air at all means real damage, so it is a טרפה.

keyTerms.meaning: Sealed, a spot in the lung that air does not enter

steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a practical, hands-on test that a שוחט or בודק can actually use to check a lung.

phrases.english: Ravina said: If there is a sealed spot in the lung,
phrases.notes: A "sealed spot" is a part of the lung that stays flat when the lung is blown up.

phrases.english: we bring a knife and cut it open.
If there is pus in it,
it was surely sealed because of the pus, and it is kosher.
And if not,
we place a feather or saliva on it,
phrases.notes: Then the lung is blown up, to see whether any air reaches that spot.

phrases.english: if it bubbles, it is kosher;
and if not, it is a tereifa.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from lung colors to a new lung problem: a spot that does not fill with air.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sealed spot with pus is כשרה. Without pus, it is כשרה only if air reaches it, shown by a feather moving or saliva bubbling; otherwise it is a טרפה.

steps.title: A membrane that grew over a lung wound does not count
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף rules that a membrane that formed because of a wound in the lung is not treated as a real membrane.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: A membrane that grew on the lung because of a wound is not considered a membrane.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives a new ruling about a lung with a wound. A layer that grew over the wound does not count as a real membrane.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a wound or hole in the lung gets covered by a new layer, you might think the hole is now sealed. רב יוסף says this layer does not count, because it only came from the wound and does not last. So the damage underneath is still treated as damage.

keyTerms.meaning: A membrane or thin layer of skin covering an organ
It is not considered a membrane

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
A membrane that grew because of a wound in the lung
is not a membrane.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ruling in the series about checking lungs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A membrane that formed because of a wound in the lung does not count as a membrane, so it does not fix the damage.

steps.title: How to check a lung that makes a whistling sound
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains how to check a whistling lung. If we know where the sound comes from, we put a feather, straw or saliva there. If we do not know, we put the lung in a basin of lukewarm water.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף also said: If a lung whistles and we know where the sound comes from, we put a feather, straw or saliva on that spot. If it bubbles, the animal is a טרפה. If not, it is כשרה. If we do not know where the sound comes from, we bring a basin of lukewarm water and put the lung in it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives a practical way to check a lung that makes a whistling noise when it is blown up. He gives one method for when we know where the noise comes from and another for when we do not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A whistling noise might mean there is a hole. If the spot is known, the feather, straw or saliva shows whether air is really escaping: bubbling or movement means a hole goes all the way through, so it is a טרפה. If the spot is unknown, the water lets us see bubbles from anywhere on the lung.

keyTerms.meaning: That makes a whistling or hissing sound

phrases.english: And Rav Yosef said:
This lung that makes a whistling sound,
if we know where it makes the sound,
we put a feather on it,
or straw, or saliva.
If it bubbles, it is a tereifa,
and if not, it is kosher.
And if we do not know where it is,
we bring a basin of lukewarm water
and place it inside.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף הַאי רֵיאָה דְּאָוְושָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second ruling of רב יוסף. Like רבינא's method in step 13, it uses a feather or saliva to test a lung.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Check a whistling lung with a feather, straw or saliva at the known spot, or in lukewarm water if the spot is unknown. Bubbling means טרפה, and no bubbling means כשרה.

steps.title: Why the water must be lukewarm
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why the water must be lukewarm. Hot water makes the lung shrink, and cold water makes it hard.
steps.simpleTranslation: Not in hot water, because it makes the lung shrink. Not in cold water, because it makes the lung hard. Rather, we check it in lukewarm water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the detail from the last step: why the water has to be lukewarm and not hot or cold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hot water would make the lung shrink, which could close up a hole so it stops bubbling. Cold water would make the lung hard and spoil the check. Only lukewarm water gives an honest result.

phrases.english: Not in hot water, because it makes the lung shrink;
not in cold water, because it makes the lung hard;
rather, we check it in lukewarm water.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the basin in step 15 must hold lukewarm water.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The check must be done in lukewarm water, because hot water makes the lung shrink and cold water makes it hard.

steps.title: The result of the water test and why a lung can whistle without being a טרפה
steps.stepSummary: If the water bubbles, the animal is a טרפה. If not, it is כשרה, because only the inner layer of the lung was pierced, and the whistle came from air moving between the two layers.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it bubbles, it is a טרפה. If not, it is כשרה. The lower layer was pierced but the upper layer was not, and the whistling sound is just air moving between the layers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the result of the water test. It also explains how a lung can whistle and still be כשרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lung has two layers. Bubbles in the water mean air is escaping through both layers, so the lung really has a hole and it is a טרפה. No bubbles means only the inner layer is pierced. The whistle is just air trapped between the layers, so the animal is כשרה.
steps.confusionAlert: A whistling sound does NOT automatically make the lung a טרפה. Only bubbling, which shows a hole through both layers, does. The whistle alone can come from a hole in just the inner layer.
steps.whatToRemember: A lung is a טרפה only if a hole goes through both of its layers. A whistle with no bubbles means only the inner layer is pierced, so it is כשרה.

phrases.english: If it bubbles, it is a tereifa,
and if not, it is kosher.
The lower layer was pierced,
phrases.notes: "Lower" means the inner layer of the lung, and "upper" means the outer layer.

phrases.english: the upper layer was not pierced,
and the fact that it whistles
is from the air in between them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the water test from steps 15–16 and explains a whistling lung that turns out to be כשרה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bubbling in the water means טרפה. No bubbling means כשרה, because only the inner layer is pierced and the whistle is air between the layers.

steps.title: A lung that turned to liquid inside is כשרה
steps.stepSummary: עולא quotes רבי יוחנן that a lung that can be poured out like water from a jug is כשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: A lung that pours out like water from a jug is כשרה.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא brings a surprising ruling from רבי יוחנן. Even if the inside of the lung has turned to liquid, the animal is כשרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the inside of the lung has melted away, but the outer layer is still whole. רבי יוחנן still calls the animal כשרה. This sets up the principle the גמרא will draw out in the next step.

phrases.english: Ulla said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
A lung that pours out like water from a jug,
is kosher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: a lung whose inside has turned to liquid.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A lung that has turned to liquid inside, so it pours like water from a jug, is כשרה.

steps.title: The principle: damage on the inside is not counted as missing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא learns from רבי יוחנן's ruling that he holds damage on the inside (חסרון מבפנים) is not counted as a missing piece.
steps.simpleTranslation: So we see he holds that something missing on the inside is not called 'missing.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a general rule out of רבי יוחנן's ruling. Something missing on the inside of the lung does not count as 'missing.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: A lung that is 'missing' a piece is normally a טרפה. Since רבי יוחנן calls a liquefied lung כשרה, he must hold that only a lack in the outer wall counts. A lack on the inside does not.

keyTerms.meaning: Something missing on the inside of an organ

steps.whyThisMatters: This principle is the target of the challenge in the next step.

phrases.english: Evidently he holds:
something missing on the inside
is not called missing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general principle from רבי יוחנן's ruling in step 18.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to רבי יוחנן, something missing on the inside of an organ is not counted as 'missing.'

steps.title: רבי אבא challenges עולא from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא points to the משנה that lists a lung that is 'pierced or missing' as a טרפה. 'Missing' on the outside would just be a hole, so 'missing' must mean on the inside. That would show that damage on the inside does count.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא challenged עולא: The משנה says, 'A lung that was pierced or that was missing.' What does 'missing' mean? If it means missing on the outside, that is the same as 'pierced'! So doesn't it mean missing on the inside? Learn from this that something missing on the inside IS called missing!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא attacks עולא's teaching with a משנה. He argues that the word 'missing' in the משנה must be talking about the inside of the lung.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists two separate problems: 'pierced' and 'missing.' Anything missing from the outer wall would already be a hole, so 'missing' would add nothing. Therefore 'missing' must mean the inside of the lung, which goes directly against the principle drawn from רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba challenged Ulla:
"The lung that was pierced or that was missing a piece."
phrases.notes: This is quoted from the משנה that lists the טרפות, where these make the animal a טרפה.

phrases.english: What is "missing"?
If you say it is missing on the outside,
that is the same as "pierced"!
Rather, is it not missing on the inside?
And learn from this:
something missing on the inside is called missing!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the principle drawn in step 19 from רבי יוחנן's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's report of רבי יוחנן, and the principle that something missing on the inside is not counted as missing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה lists 'missing' separately from 'pierced.' Missing on the outside would just be a hole, so 'missing' must mean on the inside. That would mean damage on the inside does make the animal a טרפה.

steps.title: The Missing Piece in the משנה Is on the Outside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'missing' in the משנה means on the outside. It is listed separately from 'pierced' to show that even רבי שמעון agrees that a hole with a missing piece makes the animal a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the משנה really means missing on the outside. You asked why that is not just the same as 'pierced'. It had to be said because of רבי שמעון, who says the animal is only a טרפה if the hole goes all the way into the airway tubes. That rule is only for a hole where nothing is missing. When a piece is actually missing, even רבי שמעון agrees the animal is a טרפה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבי אבא's challenge from Step 20. It says the משנה's word 'missing' is about the outside of the lung, not the inside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבא argued that 'missing' on the outside would just be the same as 'pierced', so the משנה must mean the inside. The answer is that the two cases are different for רבי שמעון. He is lenient about a simple hole unless it reaches the airway tubes, but he agrees that a hole with flesh missing makes the animal a טרפה. So רבי יוחנן's ruling that inside damage does not count still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually: this is how the גמרא says 'the case is truly like this'
It was needed: shows why a seemingly extra case had to be stated
The airway tubes (bronchi) inside the lung
A missing piece: flesh that is actually gone

steps.whyThisMatters: This answer keeps רבי יוחנן's view in place: damage on the inside is not counted as a missing piece.

phrases.english: No, it really means on the outside,
and as for what you said, 'that is the same as pierced' –
phrases.notes: This points back to רבי אבא's argument in the last step.

phrases.english: it was needed for the view of רבי שמעון,
who says: not until it is pierced into the airway tubes.

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי מִילֵּי נֶקֶב דְּלֵית בֵּיהּ חִסָּרוֹן,
phrases.english: That applies only to a hole with no missing piece,
but a hole that does have a missing piece –
even רבי שמעון agrees.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אבא's challenge from Step 20
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the משנה and explains why the extra case is needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Missing' must mean inside, because outside would be the same as 'pierced'
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Missing' is on the outside, and it is listed to show that even רבי שמעון agrees when flesh is missing

steps.title: רבי חנניה Rules a Liquefied Lung Kosher
steps.stepSummary: A story: while רבי חנניה was sick, the great sages visited him. They showed him a lung that poured like water from a jug, and he ruled it כשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנניה became sick. רבי נתן and all the great sages of the generation came in to visit him. They brought him a lung that could be poured out like water from a jug, and he ruled it kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that matches רבי יוחנן's ruling from Step 18. A lung that turned to liquid was ruled כשרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a real case that supports רבי יוחנן's ruling. Since the most important sages were present, the ruling carries extra weight.

keyTerms.meaning: The great sages of the generation

phrases.english: רבי חנניה became sick,
רבי נתן came in to him
along with all the great sages of the generation,
they brought before him a lung
that poured out like a jug,
and he ruled it kosher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a real case that matches רבי יוחנן's ruling
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A lung that pours out like water from a jug is כשרה

steps.title: Only If the Airway Tubes Are Still Whole
steps.stepSummary: רבא limits the ruling: a liquefied lung is כשרה only if the airway tubes are still whole.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This is only when the airway tubes are still whole.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a condition to the ruling that a liquefied lung is כשרה. It applies only if the airway tubes have not dissolved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now, the ruling sounded like any liquefied lung is kosher. רבא narrows it: only the flesh may have melted, while the tubes must still be intact. This sets up the next question: how can we tell?

keyTerms.meaning: And that is only when: introduces a limiting condition

phrases.english: רבא said:
And that is only when the airway tubes are still whole.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ruling from the story and from רבי יוחנן
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A liquefied lung is כשרה only if the airway tubes are still whole

steps.title: How Do We Know the Tubes Are Whole?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא asks רב אשי how we can tell whether the airway tubes are still whole.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא, son of רבא, said to רב אשי: How do we know?
steps.whatsHappening: A practical question about רבא's condition: how can we check whether the tubes are still whole in a lung that has turned to liquid? This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the whole lung looks like liquid, you cannot easily see the tubes. So רבא's rule needs a way to check it in practice.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: רב אחא, son of רבא, said to רב אשי:
How do we know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how to apply רבא's condition in practice
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A way to check whether the airway tubes are still whole

steps.title: Pour It into a Glazed Vessel and Look
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers: pour the lung into a glazed clay vessel. If there are white streaks, the animal is a טרפה. If not, it is כשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: We bring a glazed clay vessel and pour the lung into it. If there are white streaks in it, the animal is a טרפה. If not, it is kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a simple test. Pour the liquid lung into a glazed vessel and look for white streaks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: White streaks show that the airway tubes have dissolved too. That breaks רבא's condition, so the animal is a טרפה. No streaks means only the flesh melted, so the animal is כשרה.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with a fatal defect, which is not kosher

steps.whatToRemember: A liquefied lung is כשרה only if the airway tubes are still whole. White streaks in the poured-out liquid mean they dissolved, so the animal is a טרפה.

phrases.english: He said to him:
We bring a glazed clay vessel,
and we pour the lung into it.
If there are white streaks in it –
it is a טרפה,
and if not – it is kosher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of how to check
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Pour the lung into a glazed vessel. White streaks mean טרפה, and no streaks means כשרה

steps.title: A Shrunken Lung with Its Skin Whole
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules that a lung whose flesh has shrunk away is כשרה, as long as its outer skin is still whole.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: A lung that has wasted away, while its outer skin is still whole, is kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ruling begins. רב נחמן says a lung that shrank inside is kosher if its outer skin is still whole.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is another case of damage on the inside. Flesh is gone, but the outer skin is still intact, and the animal is still כשרה. It fits the idea that inside damage does not count as a missing piece.

phrases.english: רב נחמן said:
A lung that has wasted away
while its outer skin is still whole –
is kosher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new, related ruling about inside damage to the lung
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A shrunken lung with its outer skin whole is כשרה

steps.title: A ברייתא Supports רב נחמן
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches the same thing as רב נחמן: a shrunken lung with its skin whole is כשרה, even if the empty space would hold a רביעית. The next ruling then begins with the word ניטלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this: A lung that has wasted away while its outer skin is still whole is kosher, even if the empty space could hold a רביעית. If it was removed...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up רב נחמן. It adds that even a large empty space inside is fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא matches רב נחמן's ruling and goes further. Even when a lot of flesh is gone, enough to leave room for a רביעית, the lung is still כשרה if the skin is whole. The last word starts a new ruling that continues further on the daf.

keyTerms.meaning: A quarter-לוג, a set liquid measure

phrases.english: A ברייתא also teaches this:
A lung that has wasted away
while its outer skin is still whole,
even if it holds a רביעית –
phrases.notes: He means the empty space left inside, where flesh used to be, could hold a רביעית of liquid.

phrases.english: is kosher.
If it was removed...

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב נחמן's ruling with a ברייתא
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן's ruling that a shrunken lung with its skin whole is כשרה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with the same ruling, adding 'even if it holds a רביעית'
